The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 afb7bf56f8d97111), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 27-28. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: The class in (5.6) admits a decompo- sition C∗(T, H; n1, n2) = c∗[ΔX] + Γ∗, Γ∗ ∈ ∑ a+b=2 Ra X ⊠ Rb X. (5.11) 27 One can choose c∗ by a fixed universal rule. Besides the integer parameters and the chosen weights, this rule depends only on ∫ X c2(TX), ∫ X UV (U, V ∈ {K, L1, L2, T, H}). (5.12) It gives c∗ = 0 when n1 = n2 = 0. The same rule applies on every smooth projective surface with the same data and χ(OX) = 1, whether or not the lines T, H are effective; effectivity is needed only for realizing the formula as a fixed contribution.
